title: EU Auto Package: Committee vote to relax CO₂ rules
summary: In the European Parliament, standing committees have voted on the Auto Package. The votes are seen as an indicator of whether and to what extent the so-called combustion engine ban in the EU will be softened. The result: a majority of the Industry and Transport Committees are in favour of relaxing the CO2 rules, which the so-called centrist platform had internally agreed upon shortly before.

title: First drive in the Xpeng L03: finally a Chinese EV that doesn’t beep
summary: With the L03, Xpeng brings its established strengths to a new price and size segment. Particularly in the Ultra variant, its equipment goes well beyond what many rivals offer. Given its competitive pricing, the occasional shortcoming we identified during our first test drive is easier to overlook. Deliveries in Europe are scheduled to begin later this year.

title: Audi China appoints Jeff Zhang and Rolf Michl as new dual leadership
summary: Audi is reshaping its leadership team for its China business. Starting in November, Jeff Zhang will replace Johannes Roschek as President of Audi China. Additionally, Rolf Michl, previously CEO of Audi Sport GmbH, will move to China as Chief Operating Officer.

title: Holger Scherr leaves Daimler Truck for SuperPanther
summary: Chinese e-truck manufacturer SuperPanther has appointed Dr. Holger Scherr to its European management team. Scherr will serve as Executive Vice President Europe, overseeing the establishment and expansion of the company's European operations. The appointment is a coup for SuperPanther, as Scherr joins the startup from Daimler Truck.

title: London considers mandating BEVs for new ride-hailing licences
summary: Transport for London (TfL) has launched a consultation on stricter licensing rules for ride-hailing services, such as Uber. TfL is considering requiring all newly licensed vehicles to be fully electric from 2028. Wheelchair-accessible vehicles would have a transition period until July 2030.

title: Electrify America opens its largest EV charging station to date
summary: The new charging site has opened in Orlando, Florida, and features 24 DC fast chargers capable of delivering up to 350 kW each. It's located at the Sand Lake Corners South shopping centre and serves both local drivers and visitors travelling to nearby attractions, including Disney World and Universal Studios.

title: India: Switch Mobility starts fulfilling 50-unit intercity electric bus order
summary: Switch Mobility has delivered six intercity electric buses to Purple Bus, the operating brand of Pune (Maharashtra)-based Indian private bus operator Prasanna Purple Mobility Solutions. These buses form the first batch of a 50-unit order the company announced in August.

title: Greater range at the same weight: silicon battery passes laboratory test
summary: A critical breakthrough in battery research saw film cells with silicon-rich anodes endure over 1,000 cycles in testing without dropping below 80 per cent capacity. We explore the parameters that play a key role and what this progress could mean for electric vehicles.

title: Nvidia embraces European automakers
summary: Nvidia is expanding its business with technologies for automated driving in Europe. For example, the ridesharing service Bolt is relying on the Alpamayo stack from the AI company for its planned robotaxis, and VWN is showcasing the ID. Buzz AD with Nvidia Hyperion. At the same time, Volkswagen, Porsche, and other partners are advancing a joint data and simulation platform.

title: GM announces new efficient EV platform
summary: GM has streamlined its development processes and introduced a new platform in a shorter timeframe, with the first production vehicles set to debut "very soon". From 2028, vehicles on the platform will also feature significantly more efficient batteries and a faster, centralised computing system.

title: Bosch bets on electric drives for trucks – while still backing hydrogen
summary: Bosch sees significant growth potential in the commercial vehicle sector and aims to broadly support the technological transformation of trucks. At the IAA Transportation, Jan-Oliver Röhrl, Executive Vice President Commercial Vehicles and Off-Road at Bosch, spoke with electrive about e-axles, the lack of charging infrastructure, hydrogen - and why Europe should not rule out options too early when it comes to new technologies.

title: CATL’s Akin Li: “Whichever battery type the market demands, we’ll have it”
summary: CATL is a near-indispensable supplier to the emerging European e-truck industry, with many model series from local manufacturers running on cells or entire battery packs from the Chinese company. We met with CATL’s top manager Akin Li to explore how CATL plans to further strengthen its partnerships with Europe’s truck manufacturers.

title: BEV registrations rose sharply across Europe in September
summary: Registrations of electric cars in the EU rose sharply in September. According to ACEA, 290,117 pure electric cars were newly registered - 72.9 per cent more than in the same month last year. This put their market share at 29.9 per cent in September. Since the beginning of the year, BEVs have achieved a market share of 22.7 per cent.

title: Tesla Q3 results: full order books, but declining figures
summary: Tesla's revenue is stagnating, with the US electric car manufacturer witnessing a significant drop in profits during the third quarter. However, the Americans' car business is not doing poorly - order books are full. The reasons lie elsewhere.

title: Vilnius secures major loan for public transport electrification
summary: VVT, the public transport operator for Vilnius, continues to electrify its fleet. Thanks to €110 million from the CEB and EIB, the city can introduce 161 emission-free buses and the requisite charging infrastructure.

title: New rules make it much easier to install cross-pavement EV chargers in England
summary: Drivers in England can now install cross-pavement EV chargers without the need for planning permission, thanks to new permitted development rights. The government estimates the change could save households up to £300 in installation costs.

title: BYD adopts same partner as BMW for CKD assembly in Malaysia
summary: BYD has decided to collaborate with contract manufacturer Inokom on local assembly of electric cars in Malaysia. The decision is likely due to significantly tightened import conditions. Inokom is also the local manufacturer of the BMW i5 for the Malaysian market.

title: CREED project: how EVs can become power grid assets
summary: Nine European partners are exploring approaches to intelligently integrate EVs, heat pumps, batteries, and other flexible technologies into the energy system. A central component of the project is the practical testing of these approaches.

title: Belgian Post fleet now features 4,165 electric delivery vans
summary: The Belgian national postal company Bpost now operates 4,165 electric delivery vans, accounting for 42 per cent of its entire delivery transporter fleet. According to the company, 1,100 new electric delivery vans have been ordered for this year alone, most of which have already been integrated.

title: Mercedes launches new driver assist system – marking a first for Germany
summary: Mercedes-Benz is introducing its MB.Drive Assist Pro system in Germany. This makes Mercedes the first automaker to offer advanced urban partially automated driving at SAE Level 2 in Germany, in addition to China and the USA. Customers with compatible models will be able to test the feature free of charge for one month.

title: GM shutters US battery assembly near Detroit
summary: General Motors is closing its battery assembly plant in Michigan. The Brownstown Battery Assembly Plant produced battery packs for Cadillac's electric flagship, the Celestiq, as well as electric motors and batteries for the plug-in hybrid Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray.

title: VW’s battery recall affects 72,700 EVs – including 10,000 in Germany
summary: A few days ago, it leaked that VW was preparing a battery recall for several ID. models. Now it’s official: due to faulty EV batteries, Wolfsburg is recalling nearly 72,700 electric cars worldwide to workshops. In Germany, 10,000 vehicles are said to be affected.

title: CATL unveils new battery solution for eHGVs
summary: CATL has presented a new swap battery system coupled with a permanently installed extra battery. The main battery offers 432 or 513 kWh and can be exchanged at swap stations. In addition, there is the permanently installed "range-extender" battery with 77 kWh, which acts as a reserve.

title: Tesla drops out of top 10 ‘most innovative’ EV manufacturers; Mercedes gains ground
summary: Rankings of the most innovative EV manufacturers in the world continue to be dominated by Chinese and German companies. The Center of Automotive Management (CAM) sees the Geely Group, the Volkswagen Group, BYD, Mercedes-Benz, and BMW among the top 10, while Tesla has dropped out.

title: Xpeng CEO hands over the keys to first L03 delivered in Europe
summary: Xpeng CEO He Xiaopeng personally handed the keys to the first European-delivered Xpeng L03 over to its new owner. A French customer received his vehicle during a ceremony in Paris. The founder’s personal involvement underscores the strategic importance of the European market for Xpeng.

title: Updates and price cuts: what’s new with the BYD Seagull
summary: The BYD Seagull is the Chinese market counterpart to the Dolphin Surf in the European market. As the Seagull, the small electric car now receives a facelift that increases its size for added comfort. Whether the same can be expected for the Dolphin Surf remains uncertain for now. Here’s what’s new with the Seagull.

title: VW’s China reboot off to a slow start
summary: Volkswagen's restart in China utilising technology from its local partner Xpeng is reportedly off to a very rocky start. According to a news agency report, VW sold less than 10 percent of its targeted volume for the first jointly developed model, the VW ID.UNYX 08. Additionally, VW is said to have once sought an alliance with BYD or Leapmotor.

title: Indonesia: BYD launches first ‘Danza’ EVs, prepares to deploy 100 Flash Chargers
summary: BYD has introduced its first 'Danza' EVs in Indonesia after renaming its premium brand Denza locally following a trademark dispute. It has also announced plans to deploy 100 Flash Chargers in the country by December, potentially the largest rollout of its new high-power charging technology in Southeast Asia.

title: Kia PV5 Passenger seven-seater now qualifies for £1,500 UK Electric Car Grant
summary: Kia's PV5 Passenger seven-seat electric people carrier is now eligible for the UK government's Electric Car Grant (ECG). This reduces its on-the-road price by £1,500 across all three trim levels.

title: Green Science Alliance opens Swiss battery recycling lab
summary: The Japanese chemical and greentech firm has opened a battery recycling laboratory at the Switzerland Innovation Park Biel/Bienne (SIPBB) in the canton of Bern. In collaboration with the Swiss Battery Technology Center, the company aims to recover cathode material from used lithium-ion batteries, which can be directly reused in new cells. The detour via individual metals is to be eliminated.
